claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements at high concentrations.
The proposed intervention is the incorporation of machine-learning-based DFT simulations.
Machine-learning-based DFT could improve the accuracy of predicted melting temperatures and other melting properties in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning-based DFT could reduce the computational cost of predicting melting properties in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach should remain valid for single-phase solid-solution alloys.
The proposed approach should remain valid when the alloy has no long-range configurational order.
Configurational entropy is the structural mediator linking the intervention to melting-property prediction.
Machine-learning-based DFT can efficiently explore the complex configurational space of high-entropy alloys.
Efficient exploration of configurational space enables more accurate prediction of melting properties.
Traditional DFT simulations represent the current baseline prediction capability.
The machine-learning-based DFT model must be properly trained and validated for the prediction gains to hold.
A key uncertainty is whether the model can capture interactions among multiple principal elements.
A benchmark should compare traditional DFT and machine-learning-based DFT across a range of high-entropy alloys.
The benchmark should measure melting temperature, latent heat of fusion, and solid-liquid interfacial energy.
The hypothesis is falsified if machine-learning-based DFT does not improve both accuracy and computational efficiency relative to traditional DFT.
